"'''Sinestro Corps War'''" is an [[American comic book]] [[Fictional crossover|crossover]] series published by [[DC Comics]] in its ''[[Green Lantern]]'' and ''[[Green Lantern Corps]]'' titles.<ref name="dc-sine">{{Cite book | last = Wallace | first = Dan | contribution = The Sinestro Corps War | editor-last = Dougall | editor-first = Alastair | title = The DC Comics Encyclopedia | pages = 146 | publisher = [[Dorling Kindersley]] | place = New York | year = 2008 | isbn = 978-0-7566-4119-1 | oclc = 213309017}}</ref> Written by [[Geoff Johns]] and [[Dave Gibbons]] and drawn by [[Ivan Reis]], [[Patrick Gleason (artist)|Patrick Gleason]], and [[Ethan Van Sciver]], the 11-part saga was originally published between June and December [[2007 in comics|2007]]. In addition to the main storyline, four supplemental "Tales of the Sinestro Corps" one-shot specials and a ''[[Blue Beetle]]'' tie-in issue were concurrently released.

The story centers on the Green Lanterns of Earth—[[Hal Jordan]], [[Kyle Rayner]], [[John Stewart (character)|John Stewart]] and [[Guy Gardner (character)|Guy Gardner]]—and the rest of the Green Lantern Corps as they fight an interstellar war against the [[Sinestro Corps]], an army led by the former Green Lantern [[Sinestro]] who are armed with [[Green Lantern Corps#Yellow / Fear|yellow power rings]] and seek a universe ruled through fear. A 1986 [[Alan Moore]] "Tales of the Green Lantern Corps" story was the thematic basis of the storyline. Many characters were changed, killed off, or re-introduced as a result of the event.

Critical and fan reception to "Sinestro Corps War" was highly positive. Many reviewers ranked it among the top comic books of the year, and the storyline's first issue garnered a 2008 [[Eisner Award]] nomination for Best Penciller/Inker or Penciller/Inker Team. The storyline was also a financial success, and several issues underwent multiple printings. "Sinestro Corps War" is the second part of a trilogy in the Green Lantern storyline, preceded by the 2005 miniseries ''[[Green Lantern: Rebirth]]''. The conclusion of "Sinestro Corps War" sets up the third and final part of the trilogy, ''[[Blackest Night]]'', which was published in 2009.

== Plot ==

[[File:GL14.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Prominent members of the Sinestro Corps, including (clockwise from top left): the [[Cyborg Superman]] (Hank Henshaw), [[Superman-Prime]], the [[Anti-Monitor]], [[Parallax (character)|Parallax]] (Kyle Rayner), and [[Sinestro]]. Art by [[Ethan Van Sciver]].]]

Following his defeat in ''[[Green Lantern: Rebirth]]'', the events of ''Green Lantern: Sinestro Corps Special'' #1 see the supervillain [[Sinestro]] retreat to the planet [[Qward]] in the Antimatter Universe. There he amasses an army, the [[Sinestro Corps]], that he selects based on their ability to "instill great fear". Each member is armed with a yellow power ring, mirroring the green ones of the [[Green Lantern Corps]]. Amongst Sinestro's allies are [[Parallax (character)|Parallax]] and the resurrected [[Anti-Monitor]]. The Sinestro Corps then launched an all-out assault against the Green Lantern Corps and the universe itself.<ref name="dc-sine"/>

During the assault on [[Oa (comics)|Oa]], the Sinestro Corps manages to inflict heavy casualties and free [[Superman-Prime]] and the [[Hank Henshaw|Cyborg Superman]] from their imprisonment. [[Kyle Rayner]] is captured and transported to Qward, where Sinestro manages to separate Kyle from the [[Symbiosis|symbiotic]] entity [[Ion (DC Comics)|Ion]]. This allows Parallax to possess Kyle.<ref>[[Geoff Johns]] (w), [[Ethan Van Sciver]] (a), Moose Baumann (col), Rob Leigh (let). "Sinestro Corps, Prologue: The Second Rebirth". ''Green Lantern: Sinestro Corps Special'' #1 (Aug 2007), [[DC Comics]].</ref> In ''Green Lantern'' (vol. 4) #21, the heroes [[Hal Jordan]], [[John Stewart (character)|John Stewart]] and [[Guy Gardner (character)|Guy Gardner]] attempt to rescue Kyle, but are themselves entrapped, with Hal transported to face Sinestro and his allies.<ref>[[Geoff Johns]] (w), [[Ivan Reis]] (p), Oclair Albert (i). "Fear and Loathing". ''Green Lantern'' (vol. 4) #21 (Sept 2007), [[DC Comics]].</ref> A failed bid to rescue Hal depicted in ''Green Lantern'' (vol. 4) #22 sees surviving members of the Green Lantern Corps forced underground and split into two groups.<ref>[[Geoff Johns]] (w), [[Ivan Reis]] (p), Oclair Albert (i). "Running Scared". ''Green Lantern'' (vol. 4) #22 (Oct 2007), [[DC Comics]].</ref> While one group attempts to free Hal only to find themselves ambushed, the other successfully rescues Ion. They then re-unite with their ambushed comrades and together they escape from Qward back to the positive matter universe. Hal, John, and Guy return to Earth to warn the [[Justice League of America|Justice League]] of the Anti-Monitor's return.

As the Sinestro Corps spreads out to ambush Green Lanterns across the universe, ''Green Lantern'' (vol. 4) #23 sees the [[Guardians of the Universe|Guardians]] decide to rewrite their sacred text, the Book of Oa. They remove a section devoted to a prophecy concerning the "Blackest Night", against the objections of two of their number, [[Ganthet]] and [[Sayd]]. They then add ten new laws, the first of which authorizes the use of lethal force against the Sinestro Corps, while Ganthet and Sayd are expelled from Oa. As the Green Lanterns gather on Oa in preparation for a Sinestro Corps assault, the Sinestro Corps teleport themselves and their Central Power Battery instead to a new [[Warworld (DC Comics)|Warworld]], their objective revealed to be Earth.<ref>[[Geoff Johns]] (w), [[Ivan Reis]] (p), Oclair Albert (i), Moose Baumann (col). "Broken Laws". ''Green Lantern'' (vol. 4) #23, [[DC Comics]].</ref> Events in ''Green Lantern Corps'' (vol. 2) #16 show Hal informing the Green Lantern Corps of Sinestro's plans.<ref name="glc16">[[Dave Gibbons]] (w), [[Patrick Gleason (artist)|Patrick Gleason]] (p), Prentiss Rollins (i), [[Guy Major]] (col). "The Battle of Ranx". ''Green Lantern Corps'' (vol. 2) #16, [[DC Comics]].</ref>

''Green Lantern'' (vol. 4) #24 continues the story, with Green Lanterns and Sinestro Corps members battling across Earth. Hal manages to free Kyle from Parallax before the entity is imprisoned in their power batteries by Ganthet and Sayd.<ref name="gl24">[[Geoff Johns]] (w), [[Ivan Reis]] (p), Oclair Albert & Julio Ferreira (i). "Home Invasion". ''Green Lantern'' (vol. 4) #24 (Dec 2007), [[DC Comics]].</ref> After John and Guy arrive, the former Guardians reveal to them the prophecy of the "Blackest Night", seen in ''Green Lantern'' (vol. 4) #25. It foretells five more Corps arising, each based on a different color and emotion. After the five corps are established, a "War of Light" will ensue, in which all the corps are destroyed, leading to the "Blackest Night".<ref name="gl25">[[Geoff Johns]] (w), [[Ivan Reis]] & [[Ethan Van Sciver]] (p), Oclair Albert, Julio Feirreira, & [[Ivan Reis]] (i), Moose Baumann & Rod Reis (col). ''The Sinestro Corps War'' part 11. ''Green Lantern'' (vol. 4) #25, [[DC Comics]].</ref>

The Guardians arrive on Earth and appoint [[Sodam Yat]] to be the new Ion. After a lengthy struggle in [[New York City]], the Sinestro Corps are defeated by the overwhelming numbers against them. One of the Guardians sacrifices himself to send Superman-Prime to an alternate universe, and another, [[Scar (comics)|Scar]], suffers a major wound at the hands of the Anti-Monitor, while Hal and Kyle subdue and arrest Sinestro in Coast City. It is learned that 440 Green Lanterns were killed during the course of the war.<ref>''Green Lantern Corps'' #19 (Feb. 2008)</ref>

As seen in ''Green Lantern'' (vol. 4) #25, the Guardians decide to establish the second of the new laws into effect allowing the Green Lantern Corps to overpower the Sinestro Corps. After realizing that the "Blackest Night" prophecy will come to pass, Ganthet and Sayd depart after creating a [[Blue Lantern Corps|blue power ring]] with the intention of creating their own corps, based on the spreading of [[hope]] to the rest of the universe. The Anti-Monitor's remains, having been blown across the vacuum of space at the battle's climax, land on a dark planet, where they are transformed by an [[Nekron|unknown force]] into a black power battery.<ref name="gl25" />

== Origins ==
[[File:Green Lantern Corps prophecy.jpg|thumb|A page from the 1986 [[Alan Moore]]/[[Kevin O'Neill (comics)|Kevin O'Neill]] story ''Tygers'' depicting the fall of the Green Lantern Corps. Elements from the story were incorporated into "Sinestro Corps War".]]
"Sinestro Corps War" was based on concepts introduced by [[Alan Moore]] and [[Kevin O'Neill (comics)|Kevin O'Neill]] in the short story "Tygers", published in ''Tales of the Green Lantern Corps Annual'' #2 (1986). Writers [[Geoff Johns]] and [[Dave Gibbons]] incorporated several ideas from Moore's stories into "Sinestro Corps War", including the prophecy of the Blackest Night, [[Sodam Yat]], [[Ranx the Sentient City]] and the Children of the White Lobe.<ref name="Finale Newsarama">{{cite news|url=http://forum.newsarama.com/showthread.php?t=139577 |title=Happy X-Mas (War Is Over) – Geoff Johns on Green Lantern #25 |last=Rogers |first=Vaneta |work=[[Newsarama]] |date=December 13, 2007 |access-date=December 13, 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090121115426/http://forum.newsarama.com/showthread.php?t=139577 |archive-date=January 21, 2009}}</ref> Leezle Pon, a minor character only mentioned once in Moore's "Mogo Doesn't Socialize" story from 25 years prior, also makes an appearance in ''Green Lantern'' #25.<ref name="TMQ Finale">{{cite web|url=http://www.wizarduniverse.com/magazine/wizard/006702839.cfm|title=Thursday Morning Quarterback – 12/13/07|work=[[Wizard Magazine]]|date=December 13, 2007|access-date=December 13, 2007| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20071215035106/http://www.wizarduniverse.com/magazine/wizard/006702839.cfm|archive-date = December 15, 2007}}</ref>

Work began on "Sinestro Corps War" in September 2006. The structure was fluid, at one point becoming a few issues with two bookends to one longer issue.<ref name="Van Sciver Newsarama">{{cite news|url=http://forum.newsarama.com/showthread.php?t=108339|title=Tapping in to Evil: Ethan Van Sciver on Sinestro Corps|last=Rogers|first=Vaneta|work=Newsarama|date=April 11, 2006|access-date=September 3, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070716162609/http://forum.newsarama.com/showthread.php?t=108339 <!--Added by H3llBot-->|archive-date=July 16, 2007}}</ref> The title was originally just "Sinestro Corps", but during development the creators added the word "War".<ref name="green into the black">{{cite news|last=Wolk|first=Douglas|title=Geoff Johns Takes the Green into the Black|url=http://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/new-titles/adult-announcements/article/243-geoff-johns-takes-the-green-into-the-black-.html|work=[[Publishers Weekly]]|date=February 12, 2008|access-date=March 3, 2008}}</ref> Eventually, the structure finalized into a one-shot special for release in June, after which the story would alternate between ''Green Lantern'' and ''Green Lantern Corps'' until November. After the crossover's initial publishing successes, DC added four ''Tales of the Sinestro Corps'' one-shots to the publishing schedule.<ref name="DiDio"/>

Johns and Ethan Van Sciver first announced the crossover during the DC "Big Guns" panel at the 2006 [[Fan Expo Canada]],<ref name="toronto panel report 07">{{cite news|last=Weinryb|first=Avi|title=DC Comics Toronto Panel Report|publisher=Comic Book Bin|date=September 10, 2007|url=http://www.comicbookbin.com/DC_Comics_Toronto_Panel_Report007.html|access-date=September 23, 2007|archive-date=October 15, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071015082242/http://comicbookbin.com/DC_Comics_Toronto_Panel_Report007.html|url-status=live}}</ref> with Johns calling it "the next level of ''[[Green Lantern: Rebirth|Rebirth]]''".<ref name="big guns announcement">{{cite news|url=http://forum.newsarama.com/showthread.php?t=82876 |title=Toronto 06: DC Big Guns |last=Rogers |first=Vaneta |work=Newsarama |date=September 4, 2006 |access-date=October 28, 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070211012926/http://forum.newsarama.com/showthread.php?t=82876 |archive-date=February 11, 2007}}</ref> By January 2007, Johns, Gibbons, and editor [[Peter Tomasi]] had planned out most of the storyline.<ref name="dcnation76">{{cite web|last=Berganza|first=Eddie|title=DC Nation 76|url=http://www.dccomics.com/news/?nw=8463|access-date=September 3, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070905233309/http://www.dccomics.com/news/?nw=8463 <!--Added by H3llBot-->|archive-date=September 5, 2007}}</ref> Sterling Gates, whom Johns had met at a convention, was brought in to write a backup story for the Superman-Prime one-shot and co-write ''Green Lantern/Sinestro Corps Secret Files'' #1.<ref name="Sterling Gates">{{cite news|url=http://forum.newsarama.com/showthread.php?t=134069|title=Who is Sterling Gates?|last=Rogers|first=Vaneta|work=Newsarama|date=October 26, 2007|access-date=October 29, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071026021053/http://forum.newsarama.com/showthread.php?t=134069 <!--Added by H3llBot-->|archive-date=October 26, 2007}}</ref>

The creators called "Sinestro Corps War" "[[World War II]] with the entire universe".<ref name="2007 wizard gl preview">{{cite web|last=Morse|first=Ben|url=http://www.wizarduniverse.com/magazine/wizard/003000991.cfm|title=2007 Preview: Green Lantern|work=[[Wizard Magazine]]|date=January 12, 2007|access-date=October 29, 2007|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20071027070834/http://www.wizarduniverse.com/magazine/wizard/003000991.cfm |archive-date = October 27, 2007|url-status=dead}}</ref> In a September 2007 interview, Johns compared "Sinestro Corps War" to the [[Star Wars original trilogy|Star Wars trilogy]], with ''[[Green Lantern: Rebirth]]'' as ''[[Star Wars (film)|A New Hope]]'' and "Sinestro Corps War" as ''[[The Empire Strikes Back]]''.<ref name="Johns Newsarama">{{cite news|url=http://forum.newsarama.com/showthread.php?t=130914|title=A Sinestro Corps War Report|last=Rogers|first=Vaneta|work=Newsarama|date=September 27, 2007|access-date=September 27, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071011131257/http://forum.newsarama.com/showthread.php?t=130914 <!--Added by H3llBot-->|archive-date=October 11, 2007}}</ref> References to other science fiction stories were made by artist Ivan Reis, who inserted characters such as [[E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial|E.T.]], [[ALF (character)|ALF]] and a [[Predator (fictional species)|Predator]] into large two-page illustrations.<ref name="Artists Two">{{cite news |url= http://forum.newsarama.com/showthread.php?t=140469 |archive-url= https://archive.ph/20070623103614/http://forum.newsarama.com/showthread.php?t=140469 |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 23, 2007 |title=The Lantern's Artists II – Ivan Reis |last=Rogers |first=Vaneta |work=Newsarama |date=December 21, 2007 |access-date=December 21, 2007}}</ref> The writers also included the sound "EPA" in ''Green Lantern'' #25 as a direct reference to a scene in ''[[The Simpsons Movie]]'' where [[Comic Book Guy]] says it is the sound [[Hal Jordan|Green Lantern]] made when Sinestro threw him in a vat of acid.<ref name="Artists Two" />

== Format ==
The main story consisted of 11 parts running through the ''Green Lantern'' and ''Green Lantern Corps'' books. Expanding upon the overall story are four one-shots labeled ''Tales of the Sinestro Corps'', as well as one tie-in with ''[[Blue Beetle (Jaime Reyes)|Blue Beetle]]'' #20.<ref name="dcnation76"/> Part One, the one-shot ''Green Lantern: Sinestro Corps Special'' #1, was released in June 2007. Parts Two through Ten were released between August and December, alternating between ''Green Lantern'' #21–25 and ''Green Lantern Corps'' #14–18, with an epilogue in ''Green Lantern'' #26.<ref name="dcnation76"/> The content of ''Green Lantern Corps'' #19 was changed to illustrate the battle between Sodam Yat and Superman-Prime in response to the fans' reaction to the story. The conclusion of ''Green Lantern'' #25 was delayed by two weeks.<ref name="gl25 delay">{{cite news|last=Brady|first=Matt|url=http://forum.newsarama.com/showthread.php?t=133962|title=Johns Addresses GL #25 Shipping Slip|work=Newsarama|date=October 23, 2007|access-date=October 29, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071026021344/http://forum.newsarama.com/showthread.php?t=133962 <!--Added by H3llBot-->|archive-date=October 26, 2007}}</ref> After the storyline concluded, ''Green Lantern/Sinestro Corps [[Secret Files and Origins]]'' #1 was released in December. The issue further explored the back story of the opposing groups<ref name="Newsarama Dec Solicits">{{cite news|url=http://www.newsarama.com/dcnew/Dec07/solicitations.html|title=DC Comics Solicitations for December 2007|work=Newsarama|date=September 17, 2007|access-date=September 17, 2007|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20071011162221/http://www.newsarama.com/dcnew/Dec07/solicitations.html |archive-date = October 11, 2007|url-status=dead}}</ref> and listed every member of the Green Lantern Corps and Sinestro Corps.<ref name="Johns Newsarama"/>
[[File:TotSC Superman Prime cover.jpg|thumb|left|Cover to ''Tales of the Sinestro Corps: Superman-Prime'' #1, one of four one-shot issues about specific members of the Sinestro Corps. Art by [[Ethan Van Sciver]].]]

There was much internal discussion at DC about how the storyline would be collected.<ref name="green into the black"/> Eventually DC decided to release two hardcover volumes (a February 2008 release containing the first five parts of the story<ref name="comic brief oct 12">{{cite news|url=http://forum.newsarama.com/showthread.php?t=131633|title="Green Lantern" #23 and "Tales of the Sinestro Corps: Parallax" #1 Get New, Second Printings|work=Newsarama|date=October 3, 2007|access-date=April 12, 2008}}{{dead link|date=July 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} </ref><ref name="Newsarama Oct Solicits"/> and a June 2008 release containing the last six issues<ref name="TPB Solicits">{{cite news |url= http://forum.newsarama.com/showthread.php?t=139505 |archive-url= https://archive.ph/20070623103614/http://forum.newsarama.com/showthread.php?t=139505 |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 23, 2007 |title=DC Announces Trade and Collected Editions Through June 2008 |work=Newsarama |date=December 12, 2007 |access-date=December 21, 2007}}</ref>) and a June 2008 hardcover collecting the tie-in issues and backstories. This follows DC Comics' recent trend of releasing durable hardcover collections initially, followed later by softcovers.<ref name="green into the black"/>

=== Tales of the Sinestro Corps ===
In addition to the main story, DC released four ''Tales of the Sinestro Corps'' one-shots in September, October and November 2007.<ref name="dcnation76"/> The issues were late additions to the crossover that DC added after the initial successes of "Sinestro Corps War".<ref name="DiDio"/> A hardcover collection of the four issues was released in June 2008.<ref name="TPB Solicits"/> The ''Tales of the Sinestro Corps'' one-shots focused on:
* [[Parallax (character)|Parallax]], written by [[Ron Marz]] and illustrated by [[Adriana Melo]] and Marlo Alquiza.<ref name="Newsarama Sept Solicits">{{cite news|url=http://www.newsarama.com/dcnew/Sept07/solicitations.html|title=DC Comics Solicitations for September 2007|work=Newsarama|date=June 18, 2007|access-date=September 3, 2007|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070929124712/http://www.newsarama.com/dcnew/Sept07/solicitations.html |archive-date = September 29, 2007|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* [[Hank Henshaw|Cyborg Superman]], written by [[Alan Burnett]] and illustrated by Patrick Blaine and Jay Leisten.<ref name="Newsarama Oct Solicits">{{cite news|url=http://www.newsarama.com/dcnew/Oct07/solicitations.html|title=DC Comics Solitications for October 2007|work=Newsarama|date=July 15, 2007|access-date=September 3, 2007|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070903132837/http://www.newsarama.com/dcnew/Oct07/solicitations.html |archive-date = September 3, 2007|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* [[Superman-Prime]]<ref name="Antimonitor Title Change">{{cite news|url=http://forum.newsarama.com/showthread.php?t=127206|title=DC Announces Showcase Presents Changes|work=Newsarama|date=August 29, 2007|access-date=September 27, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070911175917/http://forum.newsarama.com/showthread.php?t=127206 <!--Added by H3llBot-->|archive-date=September 11, 2007}}</ref> (previously solicited as about the [[Anti-Monitor]]<ref name="Newsarama Oct Solicits"/>), written by Geoff Johns and illustrated by [[Pete Woods]]. The issue also featured the backup story "Fear is a Baby's Cry" written by Sterling Gates and illustrated by [[Jerry Ordway]].
* [[Ion (DC Comics)|Ion]], written by Ron Marz and illustrated by Michael Lacomb.<ref name="Newsarama Nov Solicits">{{cite news|url=http://www.newsarama.com/dcnew/Nov07/solicitations.html|title=DC Comics Solicitations for November 2007|work=Newsarama|date=August 20, 2007|access-date=September 3, 2007|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070929134014/http://www.newsarama.com/dcnew/Nov07/solicitations.html |archive-date = September 29, 2007|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Story and character changes ==
"Sinestro Corps War" introduced the [[Sinestro Corps]] in full after allusions to them throughout the post - [[One Year Later (comics)|One Year Later]] ''Green Lantern'' title. [[Sinestro]] received a major thematic overhaul as a result of his leadership of his eponymous Corps, with parallels drawn with [[Adolf Hitler]] and [[Nazi Germany]].<ref name="Van Sciver Newsarama"/> Green Lantern villains Superboy-Prime (later Superman-Prime), Cyborg Superman, and the Manhunters became members of the Sinestro Corps. The Anti-Monitor also made his first reappearance since his death at the conclusion of ''[[Crisis on Infinite Earths]]'' in 1985 as the "Guardian" of the Sinestro Corps and later the power source of the [[Black Lantern Corps]].<ref name="Artists One"/> Superboy-Prime was renamed Superman-Prime during the event. Ostensibly to illustrate his coming of age in the story, Geoff Johns cited the ongoing [[Superboy#Legal status|legal dispute over the Superboy name]] as another reason for the character's new name.<ref name="Johns Newsarama"/>

Some changes were also made to the heroes during the course of the storyline. The role of [[Ion (DC Comics)|Ion]] passed from [[Kyle Rayner]] to [[Sodam Yat]], making Yat the "strongest Green Lantern in the universe" as a result according to Johns.<ref name="Finale Newsarama"/> The Book of Oa was rewritten by the Guardians to institute 10 new laws for the Green Lantern Corps, the first of which authorized lethal force against the Sinestro Corps.<ref name="Johns Newsarama"/> The rebirth of [[Coast City]], the process of which had been seen throughout Geoff Johns' run on ''Green Lantern'', as "the City Without Fear" was used to symbolically represent Hal Jordan's journey towards acceptance after his resurrection.<ref name="Finale Newsarama"/> The second volume of the story's collection revealed that the original plan was for both John Stewart and Guy Gardner to be possessed by Parallax, with artwork of them facing off against Hal Jordan. However, in the midst of the story planning, Johns realized this would make Parallax's possession of Kyle less effective and the segment was dropped and redrawn.{{cn|date=February 2026}}

''Green Lantern'' #25 expanded on the "emotional spectrum" concept and introduced five [[Green Lantern Corps#Other Lantern Corps|new color-based corps]] of similar structure to the Green Lanterns and the Sinestro Corps. These corps each draw from different emotions, corresponding with the seven colors of the [[rainbow]] (red for rage, orange for avarice, yellow for fear, green for willpower, blue for hope, indigo for compassion and violet for love). [[Ganthet]] and Sayd, two [[Guardians of the Universe]] who were exiled during the course of the war, were shown as developing the corps that corresponds to the color blue and the emotion hope, while the Anti-Monitor becomes the power source for an eighth color-based corps, the "Black Lanterns", who represent death and the "absence of human drives and emotions".<ref name="Artists One"/> The issue also laid the foundations for the 2009 event ''[[Blackest Night]]'',<ref name="Finale Newsarama"/> something the creators had been working towards since early 2007.<ref name="Artists One"/>

== Critical and financial reception ==
Altogether, "Sinestro Corps War" turned ''Green Lantern'' into one of DC Comics' most profitable titles.<ref name="market watch aftermath">{{cite news|last=Paggi|first=David|title=Market Watch: Comics – Jan. 3|work=[[Wizard Magazine]]|date=January 3, 2008|url=http://www.wizarduniverse.com/magazine/wizard/006942324.cfm|access-date=January 7, 2008|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080106053618/http://www.wizarduniverse.com/magazine/wizard/006942324.cfm |archive-date = January 6, 2008|url-status=dead}}</ref> ''Green Lantern: Sinestro Corps Special'' #1, first released in June 2007, sold out in a single day.<ref name="ign june">{{cite web|last=IGN|author-link=IGN|title=Sinestro Corps Conquers Retail|date=June 29, 2007|url=http://comics.ign.com/articles/800/800693p1.html|access-date=September 3, 2007|archive-date=February 7, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120207151428/http://comics.ign.com/articles/800/800693p1.html|url-status=live}}</ref> DC later reprinted the issue four times, each time with new [[variant cover]]s by Van Sciver.<ref name="ign august">{{cite web|last=IGN|author-link=IGN|title=Sinestro Demands More Reprints|date=August 27, 2007|url=http://comics.ign.com/articles/816/816170p1.html|access-date=September 3, 2007|archive-date=February 7, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120207151435/http://comics.ign.com/articles/816/816170p1.html|url-status=live}}</ref> By August, the issue had sold over 89,000 copies, 36% of which was the result of an unusually high number of reorders.<ref name="Mayo Report Aug07">{{cite news|last=Mayo|first=John|title=Mayo Report: August, 2007 Sales Analysis|publisher=CBR News|date=October 4, 2007|url=http://www.comicbookresources.com/?page=article&id=11625|access-date=October 6, 2007|archive-date=October 26, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081026235244/http://www.comicbookresources.com/?page=article|url-status=dead}}</ref> The first four parts of the storyline, ''Green Lantern'' #21 and 22, and ''Green Lantern Corps'' #14 and 15, were released in July and August and also sold out. The issues went to a second printing, with ''Green Lantern Corps'' #14 going to a third printing.<ref name="ign august"/> ''Green Lantern'' #23 and ''Tales of the Sinestro Corps: Parallax'' #1 later went on to second printings as well.<ref name="comic brief oct 12"/> ''Blue Beetle'' #20 saw much higher sales than usual for the title as a result of its tie-in to "Sinestro Corps War",<ref name="wizard blue beetle">{{cite news|last=Mahadeo|first=Kevin|author2=Paggi, David |title=Market Watch: Comics – Oct. 30|work=[[Wizard Magazine]]|date=October 30, 2007|url=http://www.wizarduniverse.com/magazine/wizard/006226773.cfm|access-date=November 4, 2007| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20071125140150/http://www.wizarduniverse.com/magazine/wizard/006226773.cfm|archive-date = November 25, 2007}}</ref> with sales 75% higher than in the previous month.<ref name="pw october">{{cite news|last=Frisch |first=Marc-Oliver |title=DC Month to Month Sales: October 2007 |work=[[Publishers Weekly]] |date=November 30, 2007 |url=http://pwbeat.publishersweekly.com/blog/2007/11/30/dc-month-to-month-sales-october-2007/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120713033119/http://pwbeat.publishersweekly.com/blog/2007/11/30/dc-month-to-month-sales-october-2007/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 13, 2012 |access-date=January 7, 2008}}</ref>

Critical reception to "Sinestro Corps War" was highly positive. [[IGN]].com called the story a "smash hit"<ref name="ign august"/> and ''[[Newsarama]]'' referred to it as both an "action-packed DC adventure"<ref name="Best Shots GL23">{{cite news|url=http://forum.newsarama.com/showthread.php?t=129652|title=Best Shots: JLA Wedding Special, DD 100, New Avengers, and more|last=Brownfield|first=Troy|work=Newsarama|date=September 17, 2007|access-date=September 17, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071015081659/http://forum.newsarama.com/showthread.php?t=129652 <!--Added by H3llBot-->|archive-date=October 15, 2007}}</ref> and "DC's blockbuster event of the year".<ref name="Artists One">{{cite news|url=http://forum.newsarama.com/showthread.php?t=140352 |title=The Lantern's Artists, I – Ethan Van Sciver |last=Rogers |first=Vaneta |work=Newsarama |date=December 20, 2007 |access-date=December 20, 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081211100738/http://forum.newsarama.com/showthread.php?t=140352 |archive-date=December 11, 2008}}</ref> [[Comic Book Resources]] released an editorial in mid-October 2007 entitled "Sinestro Corps War is what [[World War Hulk]] SHOULD be", citing the former's ability to keep up and gain momentum throughout despite being both twice as large and far less publicized than the latter.<ref name="cbr wwh">{{cite web|last=Cronin|first=Brian|title=Sinestro Corps War is what World War Hulk SHOULD be|publisher=[[Comic Book Resources]]|url=https://www.cbr.com/sinestro-corps-war-is-what-world-war-hulk-should-be/|date=October 15, 2007|access-date=October 31, 2007|archive-date=February 29, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120229155034/http://goodcomics.comicbookresources.com/2007/10/15/sinestro-corps-war-is-what-world-war-hulk-should-be/|url-status=live}}</ref> Comic Book Resources placed "Sinestro Corps War" on its "Best of 2007" list, and named Geoff Johns one of its "Best Writers of 2007".<ref name="cbr johns one">{{cite web|last=Renaud|first=Jeffrey|title=Geoff Johns Thinking Big in the DCU, Part I|publisher=Comic Book Resources|url=http://www.comicbookresources.com/?page=article&id=12282|date=January 9, 2008|access-date=January 11, 2008|archive-date=October 26, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081026235244/http://www.comicbookresources.com/?page=article|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2008, Ethan Van Sciver earned an [[Eisner Award]] nomination for his art in ''Green Lantern: Sinestro Corps Special'' #1.<ref name="nycc 08">{{cite news|last=Rogers|first=Vaneta|url=http://forum.newsarama.com/showthread.php?t=154830|title=NYCC '08 Floor Buzz: Ethan Van Sciver|work=Newsarama|date=April 24, 2008|access-date=April 26, 2008}}{{dead link|date=July 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} </ref>

DC Comics Executive Editor [[Dan DiDio]] praised the storyline as "the best thing that [DC Comics] put out this year. Without a doubt", and called "Sinestro Corps War" the model for crossovers in 2008 and beyond,<ref name="DiDio">{{cite news|url=http://forum.newsarama.com/showthread.php?t=140406 |title=Talking to Dan DiDio, 2007 – Part One |last=Brady |first=Matt |work=Newsarama |date=December 20, 2007 |access-date=December 21, 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090227221933/http://forum.newsarama.com/showthread.php?t=140406 |archive-date=February 27, 2009}}</ref> including "[[Final Crisis]]".<ref name="DiDio IGN">{{cite news|last=Phillips|first=Dan|title=Dan DiDio on DC's Future|publisher=[[IGN]]|date=February 11, 2008|url=http://comics.ign.com/articles/851/851191p3.html|access-date=February 16, 2008|archive-date=February 18, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080218085358/http://comics.ign.com/articles/851/851191p3.html|url-status=live}}</ref>Didio has also stated that he would like to see a direct-to-video animated "Sinestro Corps War" film similar to ''[[Justice League: The New Frontier]]''.<ref name="WWLA 08">{{cite news|last=Ching |first=Albert |title=WWLA '08: DC Comics DC Nation Panel |work=Newsarama |url=http://www.newsarama.com/WWLA/08/DCNation.html |date=March 14, 2008 |access-date=April 4, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080511204507/http://www.newsarama.com/WWLA/08/DCNation.html |archive-date=May 11, 2008}}</ref> Geoff Johns suggested elements of "Sinestro Corps War" to appear in ''[[DC Universe Online]]'', on which he was collaborating with artist [[Jim Lee]], although the comic storyline wasn't incorporated in the game.<ref name="DCUO">{{cite web|last=Renaud|first=Jeffrey|title=Geoff Johns Teams with Jim Lee on DCU Online|publisher=[[Comic Book Resources]]|url=http://www.comicbookresources.com/?page=article&id=18045|date=September 15, 2008|access-date=September 29, 2008|archive-date=October 26, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081026235244/http://www.comicbookresources.com/?page=article|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Collected editions ==
The main story was first collected in two [[Trade paperback (comics)|volumes]], but was later collected in a single volume. Miscellaneous stories were collected in an additional volume:
* ''Green Lantern: The Sinestro Corps War'' (336 pages, paperback, September 2011, {{ISBN|1-4012-3301-5}})
** ''Green Lantern: The Sinestro Corps War Volume One'' (collects ''[[Green Lantern (comic book)|Green Lantern]]'' vol. 4 #21–23, ''Green Lantern Corps'' vol. 2 #14–15, and a story from ''Green Lantern: Sinestro Corps Special'' #1; 176 pages, hardcover, February 2008, {{ISBN|1-4012-1650-1}}; softcover, May 2009, {{ISBN|1-4012-1870-9}})
** ''Green Lantern: The Sinestro Corps War Volume Two'' (collects ''[[Green Lantern (comic book)|Green Lantern]]'' vol. 4 #24–25 and ''Green Lantern Corps'' vol. 2 #16–19, 192 pages, hardcover, July 2008, {{ISBN|1-4012-1800-8}}; paperback, June 2009, {{ISBN|1-4012-2036-3}})
* ''Green Lantern: Tales of the Sinestro Corps'' (collects ''Tales of the Sinestro Corps: Parallax'' #1, ''Tales of the Sinestro Corps: Cyborg-Superman'' #1, ''Tales of the Sinestro Corps: Superman-Prime'' #1, ''Tales of the Sinestro Corps: Ion'' #1, ''Green Lantern/Sinestro Corps Secret Files'' #1, and stories from ''Green Lantern: Sinestro Corps Special'' #1 and ''[[Green Lantern (comic book)|Green Lantern]]'' vol. 4 #18–20; 200 pages, hardcover, July 2008, {{ISBN|1-4012-1801-6}}; paperback, June 2009, {{ISBN|1-4012-2326-5}})

== In other media ==
In an interview with [[Newsarama]] in 2008, [[DC Comics]] executive editor [[Dan DiDio]] expressed interest in making an animated adaptation of ''Sinestro Corps War'' as part of the [[DC Universe Animated Original Movies]].<ref name="WWLA 08" /> During the early development of the [[Green Lantern (film)#Cancelled sequel|cancelled ''Green Lantern'' sequel]] in 2012, the main plot was based on the ''Sinestro Corps War'' storyline.<ref>{{Cite web |first=Russ |last=Burlingame |url=https://comicbook.com/movies/news/report-green-lantern-2-still-happening-features-the-sinestro-corps-war/ |date=September 6, 2017 |title=Report: Green Lantern 2 Still Happening, Features the Sinestro Corps War |website=Movies |access-date=October 19, 2021 |archive-date=October 19, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211019185259/https://comicbook.com/movies/news/report-green-lantern-2-still-happening-features-the-sinestro-corps-war/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
